text: Write an `EnumSet` and show it behaving as a set with declaration order. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: System.out.println(___);            // [RED, BLUE] -- declaration order, not insertion
explanation: Verified: `[RED, BLUE]`, `[]`, `[RED, BLUE]`. Note the first line: the constants were supplied BLUE-then-RED and printed RED-then-BLUE, because an `EnumSet` is a bit field over the ordinals and iterates in declaration order. For an enum of 64 or fewer constants the whole set is one `long`, so membership is a bit test and union is an OR — dramatically faster than `HashSet` and free to adopt.
